==English== ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|id=go}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*sent- (go)}} From {{inh|en|enm|senden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sendan|t=to send, cause to go}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sandijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sandijaną}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro||*sont-eye-ti|t=to cause to go}}, causative of {{m|ine-pro|*sent-|t=to walk, travel}}. The noun derives from the verb. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|stq|seende|t=to send}}, {{cog|nl|zenden|t=to send}}, {{cog|de|senden|t=to send}}, {{cog|da,nb|sende|t=to send}}, {{cog|fo,is,nn|senda|t=to send}}, {{cog|sv|sända|t=to send}}. Related also to {{cog|ang|sand}}, {{m|ang|sond|t=a sending, mission, message}}. See also [[sith]]. {{col-bottom}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|sĕnd}} * {{IPA|en|/sɛnd/|a=RP,GA,CA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-send.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-to send.ogg|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/sɪnd/|a=US,pin-pen}} * {{IPA|en|/send/|a=AU,NZ}} ** {{IPA|en|[send]|~|[se̞nd]|a=AU}} ** {{IPA|en|[se̝nd]|~|[sɪnd]|a=NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛnd|s=1}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|sent|+,~ed}} # {{lb|en|transitive|ditransitive}} To make something (such as an [[object#Noun|object]] or [[message#Noun|message]]) go from one place to another (or to someone). #: {{hypo|en|emit|broadcast|mail|post|transmit}} #: {{ux|en|Every day at two o'clock, he '''sends''' his secretary out to buy him a coffee.}} #: {{ux|en|She '''sends''' me a letter every month.}} #: {{ux|en|Some hooligan '''sent''' a brick flying through the window, and the bang '''sent''' us running out of the building.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-14|author=w:Jonathan Freedland |volume=189|issue=1|page=18|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/jun/07/obama-apple-google-facebook-tainted-prism Obama's once hip brand is now tainted] |passage=Now we are liberal with our innermost secrets, spraying them into the public ether with a generosity our forebears could not have imagined. Where we once '''sent''' love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To [[get]] one going; [[move]] to [[excitement]] or [[rapture]]; to [[delight#Verb|delight]] or [[thrill#Verb|thrill]]. #: {{syn|en|excite|Thesaurus:thrill}} #: {{usex|en|I don't know what it is, but this music really '''sends''' me.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1947|author=w:Robertson Davies|title=w:The Diary of Samuel Marchbanks|publisher=Clarke, Irwin & Co.|page=183 |passage=The train had an excellent whistle which '''sent''' me, just as Sinatra '''sends''' the bobby-sockers.}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1957|author=w:Sam Cooke|title=[[w:You Send Me|You '''Send''' Me]] |passage=Darling you '''send''' me / I know you '''send''' me}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1991|author=w:P.M. Dawn|title=w:Set Adrift on Memory Bliss |passage=Baby you '''send''' me.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|internet slang}} To [[amuse]] greatly or otherwise [[stun]] by [[absurdity]]. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[bring]] to a certain [[condition#Noun|condition]], to drive. #* {{RQ:Lawrence Sons and Lovers|[[s:Sons and Lovers/Chapter 9|chapter 9]]|passage=“I suppose,” blurted Clara suddenly, “she wants a man.”
The other two were silent for a few moments.
“But it’s the loneliness '''sends''' her cracked,” said Paul.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|usually with [[for]]}} To [[dispatch#Verb|dispatch]] an [[agent]] or [[messenger#Noun|messenger]] to find and return with a specified person or thing. #: {{syn|en|call}} #: {{ux|en|Seeing how ill she was, we '''sent''' for a doctor at once.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|2 Kings|vi|32|text=See ye how this son of a murderer hath '''sent''' to take away my head?}} # {{lb|en|transitive|sometimes followed by a [[dependent#Adjective|dependent]] [[proposition#Noun|proposition]]}} To [[cause]] to be or to [[happen]]; to [[bring]]; [[bring about]]. #: {{syn|en|bring about|bring to pass|set up}} ## {{lb|en|archaic|of a blessing or reward}} To [[bestow]]; to [[grant]]. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|I|i|passage=God '''send''' him well!}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|5|45|passage=That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and '''sendeth''' rain on the just and on the unjust.}} ##* {{RQ:Scott Waverley|passage=God '''send''' your mission may bring back peace.}} ## {{lb|en|archaic|of a curse or punishment}} To [[inflict]]; to [[visit#verb|visit]]. ##* {{RQ:KJV|Deuteronomy|28|20|passage=The Lord shall '''send''' upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke.}} # {{lb|en|nautical|intransitive}} To [[pitch#Verb|pitch]]. # {{lb|en|climbing|transitive}} To climb a route without falling. #: {{ux|en|She finally '''sent''' the 12a after hours of failed attempts.}} # {{lb|en|slang}} To pursue (a course of action) committedly, enthusiastically, and often recklessly; [[go for]]. #* {{RQ:Twitter|en|date=29 January 2024|handle=JeffSullivan__|id=1752114773255172590|passage=There is often brilliance in just saying screw it. Acting on intuition. Following the gut. Just doing it. '''Sending''' it and seeing what happens.}} #* {{quote-av|en|date=4 Jan 25|author={{w|Trevor Rainbolt}}|title=you gotta be kidding|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-7UZX6WCeig|time=2:10|passage=Why is my first instinct Spain here? Like if I was playing two seconds I would've just instant-'''sent''' Spain on this. But I think it―there's a part of me that thought it could've been Italy. But, I don't really know.}} # {{lb|en|Nigeria|slang|intransitive}} To [[care#Verb|care]]. {{rfex|en}} # {{lb|en|UK|slang}} To [[call out]] or [[diss]] a specific person in a [[diss track]]. #* {{quote-song|en|date=2017-11-07|artist=Soph Aspin|title=Courtney Jade Reply (Freestyle)|url=https://genius.com/Soph-aspin-courtney-jade-reply-freestyle-lyrics|passage=But if you want beef, it's war. I'll rip you to shreds and '''send''' once more{{...}}And you think you can '''send''' for Aspin? Sort it, stop gassing.}} # {{lb|en|Singapore|transitive}} To [[give someone a lift|give (someone) a lift]], to [[drive]] (someone) to another place. #* {{quote-web|en|author=MPH Rubin (Judge)|date=15 October 2001|title=Public Prosecutor v Khwan-On Nathaphon|work=elitigation.sg|quotee=Khwan-On Nathaphon|format=Judgment Text, CC 4/2001, Exhibit P-131 - statement recorded on 15 June 2000|location=w:High Court of Singapore|text={{...}} After closing the door, I shifted to the extreme right and sat directly behind the taxi driver. I told the driver to '''send''' me to Pasir Ris by saying "Pasir Ris Dr 12", bus stop" {{...}}|accessdate=12 December 2024|url=https://www.elitigation.sg/gdviewer/s/2001_SGHC_313|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251110081910/https://www.elitigation.sg/gdviewer/s/2001_SGHC_313|archivedate=10 November 2025}} ==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}} A compound of the sources of {{af|en|be-|come}}. From {{inh|en|enm|becomen}}, {{m|enm|bicumen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|becuman|t=to come (to), approach, arrive, enter, meet with, fall in with; happen, befall; befit}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bikwemaną||to come around, come about, come across, come by}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|be|t1=about, around|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|becum||to come, arrive, reach a destination}}, {{cog|frr|bekommen}}, {{m|frr|bykommen||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|fy|bikomme||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|nl|bekomen||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|de|bekommen||to get, receive, obtain}}, {{cog|sv|bekomma||to receive, concern}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐌹𐌵𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌽||to come upon one, befall}}. Sense of "befit, suit" due to influence from {{ncog|enm|cweme}}, {{m|enm|icweme}}, see {{m|en|queem}}. Displaced Old English {{lang|ang|''[[weorþan]]''}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|a=Southern England|/bɪˈkʌm/|/bəˈkʌm/}} * {{IPA|en|a=Northern England|/bɪˈkʊm/|/bəˈkʊm/}} * {{IPA|en|/bɪˈkʌm/|/biˈkʌm/|/bəˈkʌm/|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-become.ogg|a=California|IPA=/biˈkʌm/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪk.əm/|a=Indic}} * {{rhymes|en|ʌm|s=2}} * {{hyphenation|en|be|come}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|become<,,became:~[dialectal],~:became[dialectal]:~n>}} # {{senseid|en|copulative}} {{lb|en|copulative|followed by an adjective or a noun}} [[begin]] to [[be]]; [[turn into]] {{q|often with permanent states}}. {{defdate|from 12th c.}} #: {{par|en|get|turn|go|come|fall|grow|wax}} #: {{ux|en|She '''became''' a doctor when she was 25.}} #: {{ux|en|The weather will '''become''' cold after the sun [[go down|goes down]].}} #: {{ux|en|The full extent of my injuries did not '''become''' evident until they tried to move me.}} #: {{ux|en|The sense ‘state or process of bearing fruit’ has '''become''' imposed on ''fruition'' as the 20c. proceeded.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she '''became''' her old self again; for, even after she had conquered her love for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|archaic|_|other than in {{m|en|become of}}}} To come about; [[happen]]; come into being; [[arise]]. {{defdate|from 12th c.}} #: {{ux|en|What '''became''' of him after he was let go?}} #: {{ux|en|It hath '''becomen''' so that many a man had to sterve.}} #* {{RQ:Dunsany Time||3|And Time went forth into the worlds to obey the commands of the gods, yet he cast furtive glances at his masters, and the gods distrusted Time because he had known the worlds or ever the gods '''became'''.}} # {{senseid|en|beseem}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[appropriate]] for. {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #: {{syn|en|befit|suit|beseem}} #:''It doesn’t '''become''' a true gentleman to speak in such a manner.'' #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|III|ii|text=Ay, lord, she will '''become''' thy bed, I warrant,
And bring thee forth brave [[brood]].}} #* '''1892''', {{w|Ambrose Bierce}}, “The Applicant,” in ''The Collected Works of Ambrose Bierce'', Volume II: In the Midst of Life (Tales of Soldiers and Civilians), New York: Gordian Press, 1966,[http://www.gutenberg.org/files/13334/13334-h/13334-h.htm#page281] #*: He was hatted, booted, overcoated, and umbrellaed, as '''became''' a person who was about to expose himself to the night and the storm on an errand of charity {{...}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1930|author=w:Duff Cooper|title=Talleyrand|page=7|publisher=Folio Society|year_published=2010 |passage=His ordination{{...}}enabled him to be independent of his parents, and to afford a manner of living which '''became''' his rank rather than his calling.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} Of an adornment, piece of clothing etc.: to look [[attractive]] on (someone). {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #: {{ux|en|That dress really '''becomes''' you.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[arrive]], [[come]] (to a place). {{defdate|9th–18th c.}}

==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:resisten}}
From {{inh|en|enm|resisten}}, from {{der|en|frm|resister}} and {{der|en|fro|resistre}}, and their source, {{der|en|la|resisto|resistere}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|sisto|sistere|cause to stand}}.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[attempt]] to [[counter]] the [[action]]s or [[effect]]s of.
#* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]]|system=PC|scene={{w|Citadel (Mass Effect)|Citadel}}|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|passage=Shepard: You could have '''resisted'''. You could have fought! Instead, you surrendered. You quit.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-28|author=w:Joris Luyendijk
|volume=189|issue=3|page=21|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control Our banks are out of control]
|passage=Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic who still '''resists''' the idea that something drastic needs to happen for him to turn his life around.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[withstand]] the actions of.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Charles Johnstone|title=The Reverie; or, A Flight to the Paradise of Fools|url=http://books.google.com.sg/books?id=1mAzAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA202|volume=2|location=Dublin|publisher=Printed by Dillon Chamberlaine|year=1762|page=202|oclc=519072825|passage=At length, one night, when the company by ſome accident broke up much ſooner than ordinary, ſo that the candles were not half burnt out, ſhe was not able to '''reſiſt''' the temptation, but reſolved to have them ſome way or other. Accordingly, as ſoon as the hurry was over, and the ſervants, as ſhe thought, all gone to ſleep, ſhe ſtole out of her bed, and went down ſtairs, naked to her ſhift as ſhe was, with a deſign to ſteal them {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=16|passage=The preposterous altruism too!{{...}}'''Resist''' not evil. It is an insane immolation of self—as bad intrinsically as fakirs stabbing themselves or anchorites warping their spines in caves scarcely large enough for a fair-sized dog.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[oppose]]; to refuse to accept.
#: {{syn|en|hold out}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To be distasteful to.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Pericles|II|iii|text=These cates '''resist''' me,}}

===Etymology 1===
Probably from {{inh|en|enm|*roven}}, a Midlands variant of Northern {{inh|en|enm|raven||to wander}}, from {{der|en|non|ráfa||to rove; stray about}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|ráfa||to wander}}, {{cog|sco|rave||to wander; stray; roam}}.
